newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine overnight rate steady for 13th day.
newsitem.headline: Philippine overnight rate steady for 13th day.

text.p: * Liquidity seen tightening in next several days
Philippine overnight rates moved in a narrow range on Thursday with the average rooted at 10.53125 percent for the 13th day due to excess liquidity.

But traders said they expected extra cash in the system to be mopped up in the next several days as the Central Bank started offering on Thursday five-day reverse repos with an interest of 10.625 percent.
"I am sure a lot of banks would go into the five-day reverse repos since these are not subject to the final witholding tax of 20 percent," said one banker.
Traders said most banks have been lending to the Central Bank in the past several days due to the dearth of other investment avenues.
Tax remittances totalling 12 billion pesos by the end of the month is also expected to put a temporary drain on the system, they said.
Volume fell to 3.804 billion pesos from 5.559 billion as lenders swamped borrowers 21 to 11.
Secondary trading in government securities was also slow as market players were waiting for the Central Bank to adjust its overnight rates, traders said.

A Reuters survey of seven banks showed three-month bills were being bought at 10.7 to 10.85 percent and sold at 10.6 to 10.7 percent; six-month bills were bidded at 11 to 11.5 percent and offered at 10.85 to 11.025 percent; and one year bills were bidded at 11.425 to 11.5 percent and offered at 11.3 to 11.4 percent.
